refutations.why: A __thiscall member with one 4-byte second argument must pop it, so its epilogue must encode RET 4 as the three bytes C2 04 00. The byte at 0x008414c6 is 0xC3, a bare RET with no imm16, so the callee pops zero argument words. Independently, the body contains no [ESP] or [EBP] operand at all, so there is no stack slot from which an argument could be read.

On x86-32 an MSVC float return travels in ST0. The complete 7-byte body contains no FPU or SSE opcode, so ST0 is never written and no float can be produced; and the only write to a return register anywhere in the body is the 32-bit dword load into EAX at 0x008414c0. The body cannot return a float.

The body contains no CALL, no branch (Jcc/JMP), no CMP, no TEST and no constant. There is nothing to call, nothing to compare and no side of a branch to take. What the body does is read one receiver word at displacement 0x154 and return it.

observed_original_abi.calling_convention_rationale: The ModRM byte of the load at 0x008414c0 is 0x81, i.e. mod=10 (a 32-bit displacement follows, so the operand is register-relative and not an absolute address), reg=000 (destination EAX), r/m=001 (base register ECX). ECX is therefore the base of the body's only memory operand, which is the shape of a register-passed receiver. The epilogue at 0x008414c6 is the single byte 0xC3, a RET with no imm16, so the callee cleans zero bytes and the caller owns the stack, which is precisely the thiscall spelling (caller cleanup); with zero stack arguments __thiscall and __fastcall emit the same bytes, and __cdecl is excluded because a __thiscall member here is the identity the ModRM fixes. Five call sites confirm the receiver role from the caller side; the decisive one is 0x00bbc340, where MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESP+0x4] moves the caller's own first stack word into ECX and CALL 0x8414c0 makes it the receiver, so ECX carries an object pointer and not a value.
observed_original_abi.receiver_type_claim: none. SporeApp.exe carries no MSVC RTTI; the receiver is an opaque, vtable-owning object reached through the slot recorded under vtable_placement. No class name is inferred from the address.
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: The machine fixes only a 32-bit word: the sole write to EAX in the whole body is the dword load MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0x154] at 0x008414c0, and the epilogue at 0x008414c6 returns it unchanged -- no sign extension, no narrowing, no re-encoding, no float conversion. NO DECLARED SEMANTIC TYPE IS CLAIMED for the word: it is not asserted to be a pointer, a handle, a bool, a count or anything else. Caller-side observations (0x00acf7c8 MOV [ESP+0xf8],EAX stores it; 0x00bbc349 and 0x010050b3 TEST EAX,EAX / JE null-test it; 0x00f35f55 and 0x00cdd896 MOV ECX,EAX and call through it) are consistent with a pointer-shaped word, but that is caller behaviour and not a declared type of the returned value.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: EAX receives the 32-bit little-endian word at receiver+0x154 bit-for-bit. It is the only register the body writes.
observed_original_abi.termination: RET at 0x008414c6, the bare single byte 0xC3 with no imm16 operand

unresolved_questions: What class owns this slot? SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI, the table's other slots carry FUN_ placeholders and four SDK-imported labels, and the exported decompilation is an artefact, so no owner is named here.

What is the 32-bit word at receiver+0x154 semantically? The body fixes its offset, width and read-only access and nothing else; 851 other [reg+0x154] sites exist in the binary, so the displacement alone identifies no member.
Does any of the 34 direct call sites pass a receiver of a different concrete type, and are all 30 caller functions reaching it through the same vtable as the slot at 0x0141c97c?

notes: Recorded from the two-instruction body (7 bytes), its raw image bytes, the .rdata word that makes it a vtable slot, and the committed xref exports. The reconstruction is total for this body: both instructions, the disp32, the ModRM decomposition, the epilogue form and the return width are accounted for and nothing is asserted beyond them. The central finding of this record is negative and is preserved rather than smoothed over: the SDK symbol attached to 0x008414c0, ArgScript::FormatParser::ParseFloat, is refuted twice by the bytes -- the bare 0xC3 at 0x008414c6 admits no callee-popped char* and the complete absence of any FPU or SSE opcode admits no ST0 float -- so the record's own identity is the address placeholder FUN_008414c0 and the SDK name appears only under refuted_symbol, with the refuting instruction named in each case. The vtable slot rests on a single .rdata image read because the xref export records no vtable-ref row for this VA, and the +0x154 displacement names no member because 851 other [reg+0x154] sites exist in the same binary. No declared semantic type is claimed for the returned word.
